option: CONTAINMENT REVIEW: There was no breach. The specimen predates the site. It grew a laboratory around itself.
text:
RECORDS ROOM SEALED FILE
${P} FINDING OF FACT

There was no breach.

We have reviewed every log. Whatever it is, IT never came IN. The anomaly predates the facility.

The facility predates the level.

We did not build a laboratory around a specimen; a specimen grew around the laboratory.

[${c.lead}'s final margin note: "We are the note it left for itself."]

option: PERSONNEL FINDING: ${c.lost} is alive. Every locked door was sealed by hand, from the inside. It is trapped WITH ${c.lost}.
text:
RECORDS ROOM SEALED FILE: ${P} "FINDING OF FACT"

Despite the insistence of HQ, ${c.lost} is alive. That is the finding. Every door that will not open has been locked FROM THE INSIDE.

We have found encouraging but archaic handwritten messages, in ${c.lost}'s handwriting, in impossible places.

This leads me to the only logicl conclusion, based on what I know:

${c.lost} is not trapped in there with it.... It is trapped in there with ${c.lost}.

[SIGNED IN RED INK]: ${c.lead}, PROJECT LEAD

option: TRANSMISSION AUDIT: The hum is a carrier wave. The building is broadcasting its own contents somewhere. The staff are the payload.
text:
RECORDS ROOM SEALED FILE
${P} FINDING OF FACT

The hum is a carrier wave. ${c.archivist} proved it in the stacks: the documents rearrange along it. The building is not haunted. The building is TRANSMITTING — inventory, floor plans, personnel files — somewhere. We are not test subjects.

We are the payload.
